clue.text: See 4
Romeo, as captured by sculptor

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Antonio Canova, the Italian neoclassical sculptor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover is caught in the act, or immortalised in marble, by an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Antonio Canova was the Italian neoclassical sculptor of Cupid and Psyche; the short word sits after his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are generic nicknames for an amorous man, after Shakespeare's lover and the Venetian adventurer famous for seductions.

clue.text: See 4
Awful pity a lout and misanthrope couldn’t care less when customer initially cut off – ‘Hello? I … ’

annotation.answer: YOUR CALL IS IMPORTANT TO US PLEASE HOLD THE LINE

definitions.text: Awful pity a lout and misanthrope couldn’t care less when customer initially cut off – ‘Hello? I … ’

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder
to cut something off is to remove it, so the letter named is struck out of the mix

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material
the opening letter, which is removed from the material
taken as written, the final scraps of anagram material

explanation.surface: A furious, abandoned caller on a telephone queue rants at the uncaring company before the line goes dead mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: One C is removed from the forty-one letters and the rest rearranged into YOUR CALL IS IMPORTANT TO US, PLEASE HOLD THE LINE. The whole clue doubles as the scenario in which that recorded message plays.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the recorded message heard by callers left waiting in a company's telephone queue, exactly the situation the clue describes.

clue.text: Passing round pub, predator has cut a dash

indicators.note: having something cut means losing it, so the named letter goes
to pass round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a hyena is a predator of the African plains
taken as written; this letter is removed
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A wild animal goes past the local and makes a quick run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut a dash' looks like the idiom for looking stylish, but 'cut a' is the instruction and 'dash' alone is the definition. PH is the map abbreviation for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a short horizontal punctuation stroke, loosely called a dash in everyday speech.

clue.text: Move, on wind coming up round both poles

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses another
in a down clue, coming up means travelling bottom to top, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: RE means concerning or on the subject of
breaking wind
S and N, the south and north poles

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to shift position as the breeze rises and swings around from north to south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like weather but is the schoolboy kind, a Paul favourite. In a down clue, 'coming up' means the whole assembly reads from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer is to shift something or someone from one place to another, a straightforward synonym for move.

clue.text: Head on couch after shows, a bit of a breather?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top, which in a down entry is its opening letter
placing one thing after another fixes the order in which the parts are joined

blocks.note: to air something is to show it publicly
taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone flops onto the sofa after a run of performances for a short rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a short rest, but here it is a creature that breathes. C goes after AIRS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Air sacs are respiratory organs in birds and insects, so one is literally a part of an animal that breathes.

clue.text: All the same, only if all sit?

blocks.note: first meaning: nevertheless, in spite of that
second meaning, read cryptically: if everyone sits, nobody is on their feet, so it splits into three words

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT WITH STANDING, the word describes a gathering where everyone is seated; the question mark flags that whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means nevertheless or despite this, the same sense as the stock phrase used for conceding a point.

clue.text: Record on prowler after probing thus has army finally dropping investigation?

indicators.note: a probe is pushed into something, so one piece goes inside another
finally points to the closing letter of the word it qualifies
in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so that piece is sent second
one piece placed after another sets the order of joining

blocks.note: so means thus, in this way
a cat prowls at night
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A night-time burglary is recorded while the army withdraws from an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like abandoning, but it means animal droppings. 'Prowler' is a cat, the classic night stalker.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatology is the scientific study of excrement, so an investigation into droppings, with the question mark flagging the pun.

clue.text: Money one might charge

blocks.note: first meaning: old British slang for cash
second meaning: a large horned animal known for charging at threats

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fee or price someone might ask; 'charge' is really an animal running at you. Rhino is dated British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for cash shares its form with the short name for the rhinoceros, a famously charging beast.

clue.text: Cruel sea rolling back in drift

indicators.note: something rolling back travels the way it came, so its letters run right to left

blocks.note: mean means unkind or cruel
the Red Sea

explanation.surface: A merciless ocean surges back as a boat is carried off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruel sea' reads as one phrase (Monsarrat's novel), but it splits into a synonym and a named sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly without a fixed course, much as one might drift along.

clue.text: Tool within Shaw novel?

blocks.note: surface reading: an implement turning up in a book by George Bernard Shaw
setter's reading: the answer splits into the letter H, the word 'and' and a cutting tool, and those two outer pieces jumbled make Shaw

explanation.surface: A reader spots a piece of equipment hidden somewhere in one of Shaw's books.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as H AND SAW: H and SAW rearranged give SHAW, with the saw itself inside the phrase. The question mark warns that the wordplay is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsaw is a carpenter's cutting implement used with one hand, so it is a type of tool.

clue.text: First of all one’s blasted, or else one’s blown

indicators.note: the first of every word means taking the opening letter from each in turn

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Either something gets blasted or it gets blown, whichever comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters spell the answer, and the clue also hints at the woodwind instrument being played loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, played by a musician breathing air through it.

clue.text: Hymn I’m fanatic about, good parts

indicators.note: to part is to split up, so these letters are separated and rearranged
about means surrounding, so one piece sits around another

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A churchgoer admits obsessive devotion to a particular song, at least its better sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters are split around G. 'Parts' looks like a noun meaning sections but works as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificat is the canticle of the Virgin Mary sung at evensong and vespers, a well-known Christian hymn of praise.

clue.text: Emotional time before reprimand

indicators.note: placing one thing before another sets the order of joining

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an earful is a telling-off

explanation.surface: Someone gets upset just before receiving a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: An earful is British informal for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tearful means close to crying, an outward sign of being moved or upset.

clue.text: Sellers of bunches, fifty however in bunch of five items?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
or here means otherwise, a loose sense of however
a fist is a bunch of five fingers, made plural

explanation.surface: Market traders selling bouquets in sets of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunch of five' is crossword slang for a fist, since five fingers are bunched together. 'However' gives OR in its sense of otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Florists sell cut flowers, usually arranged into bouquets, which are commonly called bunches.

clue.text: Yards away from cypress, and poplar removed from popular new trees

indicators.note: whatever is away from a place is absent from it, so these letters go missing
something new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word, which is then taken out
taking the letters of the shorter tree out of the longer word leaves a single letter

explanation.surface: A gardener clears out the cypress and poplar to plant fashionable new trees.
explanation.walkthrough: CYPRESS without Y gives CPRESS; POPULAR without POPLAR leaves U. The seven letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruces are evergreen conifers, so they are a kind of tree, defined here by the general class.

clue.text: Nothing’s broken as in rebuilt country

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
to have broken into something is to get inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Nothing is damaged in a nation rebuilt after war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' looks like damage but means broken in; LOVE goes inside a rearrangement of AS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe, formerly part of Yugoslavia, so it is a country.

clue.text: Where a corpse originally buried in a crypt beneath surface of chamber?

definitions.text: Where a corpse originally buried in a crypt beneath surface of chamber?

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its beginning, so take the opening letter
in a down clue the surface is the top, which is the opening letter
something buried in something else lies inside it
in a down entry, what lies beneath comes later, fixing the order of the parts

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
the opening letter of the word
a tomb is a burial vault, like a crypt

explanation.surface: A question about where a body was first laid to rest beneath a vault.
explanation.walkthrough: A and C go inside A TOMB, and C sits on top. The whole clue also describes an underground burial chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery of tunnels and recesses, the very place a body would be laid below ground.

clue.text: Pillock, new money ultimately spent before business done?

indicators.note: its final part used up means the last letter is lost
placing one thing before another sets the order of joining

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
income is money earned
doing one's business is a euphemism for defecating

explanation.surface: A fool blows fresh cash before a deal is completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business done' looks like a completed deal but is a toilet euphemism. Pillock is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal, mildly insulting words for a foolish or stupid person, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Hand, or spleen?

blocks.note: first meaning: the pointer on a dial or gauge
second meaning: irritation or hostility

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a choice between two body parts; each word has a non-anatomical meaning instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the pointer of an instrument, and in British usage needle also means ill feeling or provocation.

clue.text: See 4
Corridor linking capitals of Switzerland and Austria?

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its opening capital letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
the word 'to' links two places
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A transport route connecting Bern and Vienna through the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' tempts you towards Bern and Vienna, but it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greek architecture, essentially a sheltered walkway.

clue.text: See 4 Down
Tempted to have hospital department decorated

blocks.note: ear, nose and throat department
a cake is decorated with icing

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to get a ward smartened up.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the standard abbreviation for the ear, nose and throat department.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to lure them by offering something attractive, which is to tempt them.

clue.text: River kid mentioned?

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child is spoken of near a watercourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the verb meaning to joke with. The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a named English waterway flowing into the North Sea at Middlesbrough, so it is a river.

clue.text: Dark – otherwise with second opening?

blocks.note: surface reading: an alternative involving a second gap or doorway
setter's reading: put S, for second, at the front and the word becomes its opposite, bright with daylight

explanation.surface: Gloom, unless a second window lets in light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' means the reverse: with S added at the start, the dark word becomes SUNLIT. S is the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlit means not lighted or illuminated, so a place left unlit is dark.

clue.text: Armed criminal in twist has become comic book hero

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
a spin is a twist or turn

explanation.surface: A gunman, in a plot twist, turns into a costumed superhero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed criminal' reads as a gunman; it is the anagram material and its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is the Marvel superhero, one of the best-known characters from American comics.
